question: Inspiratory stridor indicates obstruction at or above the level of the glottis (supraglottic or glottic), whereas expiratory stridor or wheeze indicates intrathoracic (lower airway) obstruction, and biphasic stridor suggests a fixed glottic or subglottic lesion.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Stridor phase anatomically localises the obstruction: inspiratory = supraglottic/glottic (extrathoracic); expiratory = intrathoracic lower airways; biphasic = fixed glottic/subglottic. Applying this rule immediately narrows the differential from the auscultation alone.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The phase of stridor is the most reliable anatomical localiser: inspiratory (extrathoracic narrowing — supraglottis or glottis, e.g. epiglottitis, laryngomalacia, croup), expiratory/wheeze (intrathoracic — bronchi, e.g. bronchiolitis, asthma, vascular ring), biphasic (fixed glottic or subglottic lesion, e.g. subglottic stenosis, haemangioma). This rule is the pivot point for triage and investigation.
